To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The presence of eight critical success factors for a performance improvement program was associated with the successful implementation of change initiatives.
the presence of critical success factors is associated with the success of a performance improvement program.

the critical success factors for performance-improvement program are: (1) A strong administrative executive and performance-improvement leader who has the support of a strong board; (2) An effective oversight structure, with an expert staff, and a physician leader who is involved and held accountable for the results of the performance-improvement effort; (3) A communication strategy that involves the staff in the process; and (4) The use of information resources for data-driven decision-making.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying and describing the organizational structures and processes that are most likely to lead to the successful implementation of performance improvement programs in health care organizations.
the identification of critical organizational factors that support the development of an effective performance improvement structure.
the design of an organizational model for PI.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a strong administrative and executive leadership is the most important success factor for a successful performance improvement program, followed closely by active involvement of the board of trustees.
a strong organizational structure and processes are necessary to support change initiatives, and that the presence of these elements will increase the likelihood of success.
a PI program is a critical success factor for an effective performance management system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there are no quick fixes to performance improvement.
the most important factor for success of an improvement program is the presence of a strong administrative executive and performance improvement leadership.
the presence of these critical success factors is associated with a more effective performance improvement program.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a PI program alone does not guarantee improvement.
the organizational context is critical to the success of performance improvement efforts.
organizations that are successful at performance improvement have a strong commitment to the process, and that commitment is reflected in organizational structures and processes.
